news.headline: Invivyd Announces Positive Topline Results from LIBERTY Phase 3 Study Demonstrating VYD2311 Safety and Tolerability Superior to mRNA-based COVID-19 Vaccine; Announces Regulatory Submission Plans for VYD2311
news.body: VYD2311 met all primary and secondary endpoints comparing VYD2311 to an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, demonstrating VYD2311 safety and tolerability that is clinically and statistically superior to the safety and tolerability of an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccineVYD2311 combined with an mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine demonstrated no interference with vaccine-induced neutralizing titers, and instead added substantially to vaccine-induced neutralizing titersVYD2311 observed profile in LIBERTY indicates high measured neutralizing antiviral titers supporting the target profile for VYD2311 under study in the DECLARATION pivotal clinical studyInvivyd plans for DECLARATION and LIBERTY clinical studies to be the basis of a planned Biologics License Application (BLA) submission for VYD2311 to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration via Accelerated Approval Program following a recent Type C meeting; DECLARATION topline data on safety and immunogenicity to support the submission are now expected in October; DECLARATION clinical efficacy data will be planned to be unblinded post-Accelerated Approval, if granted, subject to clinical event accrual Investor call to be held at 8:30 am ET on September 29, 2026 NEW HAVEN, Conn., Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Invivyd, Inc. (Nasdaq: IVVD) today announced positive, clinically meaningful, and statistically significant topline data from the LIBERTY Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, active controlled study evaluating the safety and tolerability of (1) VYD2311, Invivyd’s investigational COVID-directed monoclonal antibody candidate, (2) mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine COMIRNATY® (mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, or COVID vaccine), and (3) VYD2311 co-administered with mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. The study also evaluated the potential for immunologic interference between VYD2311 and mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine. LIBERTY is a companion study to DECLARATION, the ongoing placebo-controlled pivotal study of VYD2311 for pre-exposure prophylaxis of symptomatic COVID-19.

logs.summary: Three months after the twin earthquakes, family members and volunteers continue searching collapsed buildings for their missing loved ones, with at least 1,500 people still unaccounted for. Separately, New Zealand engineers who traveled to Venezuela to assist in the aftermath are sharing lessons on earthquake resilience, highlighting that nearly 200 buildings collapsed and more than 16,000 structures were deemed unsafe.

news.body: Sleeping in tents in front of collapsed buildings and removing rubble with bare hands, family members and volunteers search the ruins with at least 1,500 people missing.

news.headline: Kiwi engineers learn from Venezuela's devastating earthquakes
news.body: Last month, four New Zealand engineers flew to Venezuela to help in the aftermath of the devastating double quakes, which hit the western and central parts of the country in June, leaving more than 6000 people dead. Nearly 200 buildings collapsed in the quakes while more than 16-thousand structures were deemed unsafe. For the Kiwi engineers, it was a chance to learn about what New Zealand could do better, when it comes to earthquake resilience. University of Canterbury civil and environmental engineering Professor Santiago Pujol, director of the earthquake research centre, QuakeCore spoke to Ingrid Hipkiss.

news.headline: 5.5-magnitude earthquake strikes Chile after deadly twin quakes in Venezuela
news.body: A 5.5-magnitude earthquake struck Chile on Wednesday, the same day after two powerful quakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 hit central Venezuela, killing at least 32 people and leaving hundreds injured.

logs.summary: Three months after the twin earthquakes, young people from the Diocese of La Guaira gathered to remember victims in a prayer and song memorial. An AP investigation reports that scientists had warned the government against building along the La Guaira coastal strip, warnings that appear to have been ignored. Meanwhile, World Vision Venezuela provided food assistance to affected families in the Carayaca parish as part of continued humanitarian response.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. In the United States, drought conditions worsened in states like Minnesota and Michigan, while other areas like the Grand Strand in South Carolina are lifting drought management plans, and parts of Virginia and North Carolina are seeing improvements.
New drought developments include worsening conditions in Maine and Minnesota, with 35% of Minnesota in severe drought, while South Carolina's Lowcountry remains under extreme drought despite summer storms. In Europe, record-low river levels continue to disrupt power output and transport, and wildfire risk is elevated across the continent. Jamaica faces a potential $500 million drought response, and drone footage highlights the drought's impact in England.

news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
Rocky Mount, Virginia issued a voluntary water conservation request due to ongoing drought conditions, with the town receiving only about half its normal rainfall. In North Dakota, dry weather has caused hay shortages, with drought-damaged cereal crops down to 50% of normal, prompting producers to plan late-season alfalfa management. Separately, forecasters warn that the 2026-27 El Niño is strengthening into a very strong event, increasing the risk of heat and erratic rainfall.
Recent reports show drought persisting across several regions: central Minnesota's drought held steady while statewide conditions eased slightly, and eastern Idaho farmers are expecting lower potato yields due to drought and heat. Alabama's drought has been increasing, especially in southern and western areas, while St. Thomas has deteriorated into exceptional drought even as Puerto Rico saw slight improvement. Forecasts warn of a potentially unprecedented El Niño in 2026/27 that could bring below-normal rainfall to South Africa, and drought combined with the Black Sea grain crisis is raising global food security concerns, while El Niño-driven drought in Papua New Guinea has forced school sports cancellations.

logs.summary: Severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, and flash flooding impacted multiple regions across the United States from August 20–24, 2026. Confirmed tornadoes struck in Atlantic Beach (Long Island), Dover (Delaware), and York/Lancaster counties (Pennsylvania), while prolonged power outages from earlier storms left thousands without electricity in Gary, Indiana, for over a week. Widespread damage from downed trees, damaged homes, and flooding was reported in the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, and Midwest.

logs.summary: A glacier collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border triggered devastating flash floods and mudslides on August 26, 2026, sweeping through several communities in the Bagmati region. The disaster has killed hundreds of people (with death tolls reported between 350 and 500) and left over 1,300 missing, including dozens of foreign nationals. Rescue teams are searching for survivors while authorities warn of additional flood risks from a newly formed lake, and international aid is arriving to support relief efforts.

news.headline: Aug. 27: Flash Flooding Overwhelms Nepal, and Jury Deliberates in Lindsay Clancy’s Murder Trial
news.body: Devastating flash floods and mudslides wreaked havoc along the Nepal-China border this week, leaving hundreds dead and more than 1,000 missing. More than 500 foreigners are among the missing, including, by one estimate, roughly 65 Americans. NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer explains why the destruction happened without warning and what role climate change may have played. Then, jury deliberations are underway in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who killed her three young children. While Clancy doesn’t dispute the killings, her defense team is arguing that she shouldn’t be held criminally responsible because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. But the prosecution insists she acted intentionally and deliberately. As the jury weighs a set of complex outcomes, NBC News legal analyst Misty Marris breaks down what evidence and testimony from the five-week trial could be key to reaching a verdict. Finally, 2026 could be the year of the foldable phone. Samsung and Google already have models on the market, and Apple is reportedly planning to drop its version in September. But are consumers willing to shell out $2,000 for a little extra screen? NBC News chief tech analyst Joanna Stern explains why the phones have appeal.

news.headline: Fact Check: क्या पानी के तेज बहाव में बहती गाड़ियों का यह वीडियो नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा का है?
news.body: सोशल मीडिया पर नेपाल और थाईलैंड में आई बाढ़ से जोड़कर दो अलग-अलग वीडियो तेजी से वायरल हो रहे हैं. पहले वीडियो में पानी के तेज बहाव में गाड़ियों के बहने का दृश्य दिखाकर दावा किया गया कि यह नेपाल-तिब्बत सीमा पर आई बाढ़ का है. पड़ताल के दौरान वीडियो में गाड़ियों के अप्राकृतिक तरीके से तैरने और धुंधली नंबर प्लेट जैसी खामियां मिलीं. एआई डिटेक्शन टूल्स की जांच में यह वीडियो 80 से 89 प्रतिशत तक एआई जनरेटेड पाया गया. वहीं दूसरे वीडियो में थाईलैंड की राजधानी बैंकॉक में बाढ़ के पानी में सड़कों पर मछलियों के तैरने का दावा किया गया. जांच में सुविधा स्टोर के साइन बोर्ड पर गलत वर्तनी, पानी की कम गहराई और स्थिर गाड़ियां दिखाई दीं. एआई डिटेक्शन टूल ने 97 प्रतिशत संभावना के साथ इसे भी एआई जनरेटेड बताया. इस तरह दोनों वायरल दावे पूरी तरह भ्रामक और फर्जी साबित हुए.

logs.summary: Severe monsoon rains and cyclones have caused widespread flooding across the Philippines, particularly in Luzon, with damage nearing P4 billion in Central Luzon and P2.68 billion in infrastructure damage in the Ilocos Region, affecting over four million people. At least two brothers drowned in a submerged bypass road in Pampanga, and a baby was dramatically rescued from flash floods in Manila. In response, lawmakers are pushing for flood control master plan reviews and Senate investigations into the government's disaster response.

logs.summary: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensified into a Category 5 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast, becoming one of the strongest hurricanes ever recorded in the Eastern Pacific. It weakened slightly to a Category 4 but continues to bring heavy rain and life-threatening flooding and landslides to southwestern Mexico, particularly Guerrero state. The storm is expected to remain offshore, but officials warn of significant hazards from rainfall and mudslides.

logs.summary:
A weather system over the Bay of Bengal is set to make landfall between Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on September 22, 2026, with schools and liquor shops closed in Malkangiri. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center classifies it as Tropical Cyclone 01B, while the India Meteorological Department officially considers it a deep depression; social media erroneously named it "Cyclone Arnab". Red alerts and heavy rain warnings are in place for the affected areas.
The deep depression that formed over the Bay of Bengal has made landfall along the Andhra-Odisha coast. Over 1,500 people were evacuated from Gajapati district, and red alerts remain in effect as heavy rain continues.
